props.title: Home
props.initialSlug: Aerial documentary about Earth's ecological state

sections.content: **Home** (2009) revolutionized environmental documentaries through Yann Arthus-Bertrand's stunning aerial cinematography. Shot entirely from helicopters across 54 countries, it presents Earth's fragile beauty and humanity's impact with breathtaking visual poetry. This approach influenced later eco-docs like **Chasing Ice** (2012) and **Before the Flood** (2016), establishing a new visual language for environmental storytelling. The film's narrator-driven format recalls An Inconvenient Truth (2006), but trades PowerPoint presentations for spectacular bird's-eye views of our planet.

sections.content: The film's innovative approach to environmental messaging influenced a wave of visually-driven eco-documentaries. **Racing Extinction** (2015) adopted similar sweeping cinematography to document species loss, while **Salt of the Earth** (2014) used photographer Sebastião Salgado's stunning black-and-white images to explore humanity's relationship with nature. These films prove that environmental messages land stronger through visual poetry than lectures.

What sets **Home** (2009) apart is its global perspective, showing how local environmental changes connect to worldwide patterns. This holistic approach inspired later works like **This Changes Everything** (2015) and **A Beautiful Planet** (2016), which examine climate change through interconnected global systems rather than isolated issues. sections.content: The technical achievements of **Home** (2009) pushed aerial photography into new territory. Using Cineflex cameras stabilized by gyroscopes, Arthus-Bertrand captured impossibly smooth footage from helicopters, influencing films like **Samsara** (2011) and **Aquarela** (2018). This technical innovation showed that environmental documentaries could be both informative and visually spectacular.
